text:
Maya: sharing the latest compact version-history mock for rollouts — thinking about how we surface canary vs A/B variants and the rollback affordance. link: https://figma.redwood/compact-history Simon: nice. what's the main UX goal here? reduce vertical space or make quick reverts less scary? Maya: both. users want to scan recent versions quickly and restore to a prior version in 1-2 clicks. but product asked that rollback confirmation be explicit about data/traffic effects. Ben: UI nits: the timeline looks dense. propose small chips for variants: 'canary 10%' vs 'A/B: variant B'. chips should be keyboard-focusable. Rach: keyboard focus + screen reader text is critical. we need clear aria-labels for each chip and the rollback button. also contrast on the timeline divider is low. Alex: engineering constraints: the backend uses action names `rollback`, `promote`, `replay`. If copy diverges too much we risk mismatch in audit logs. prefer UI copy that maps to API verbs or include an alias. Simon: product preference is 'Revert' over 'Rollback' — less scary. But we must be consistent with logs. could we show friendly copy everywhere and keep the raw verb in the details panel? Maya: that sounds OK. suggestion: primary action label 'Revert to this version' and in the modal show 'action: rollback' in small helper text to match logs. Ben: microcopy proposal for confirm modal: header: 'Revert deployment', body: 'Reverts traffic and configuration to version 5. This will NOT delete older versions. All in-flight requests may be routed differently.' primary button: 'Revert now' secondary: 'Cancel'. add a small link 'View audit log' Rach: also include a live region update when the action completes: `aria-live=\"polite\"` with a short status message. For keyboard users, trap focus in modal and return focus to the version entry that was reverted. Alex: quick snippet for accessible slider + numeric entry for canary percentage (from prototype): ```
``` Ben: love the dual control. UX question: should we show exact numbers on the compact timeline or only on hover/details? Maya: show percent on the chip (e.g., 'canary 10%') but keep the slider in the detail flyout. chips remain tappable to open details. Simon: A/B labeling: recommend explicit variant tags 'A' and 'B' and show which metric is primary (latency, accuracy). Also add a small tooltip: 'A/B test — traffic split 50/50'. Rach: tooltip must be keyboard accessible and have role=\"tooltip\" plus aria-describedby on the chip. Also ensure color-only indicators have text alternatives. Alex: about rollback safety: backend will attempt a graceful switch. we should add a visible countdown and a 'force revert' option in the modal for emergencies. the countdown must be cancellable. Ben: visual design idea: animate a small reversible transition on the timeline entry during countdown to signal pending state (subtle motion, high-contrast border). keep motion reduced option for users who prefer reduced motion. Maya: copy tweak debate: \"Revert to this version\" vs \"Restore this version\". Which reads better for non-technical users? Simon: I vote \"Restore\" — less destructive-sounding. but clarifying subtitle: 'Restore traffic and config to this version' Alex: engineering note: if we use 'Restore' we should map it to the `rollback` action internally and show mapping in audit logs, as suggested earlier. Rach: accessibility note: whichever term we pick, ensure it's used consistently in aria-labels and confirmation messages. screen reader users should hear the same verb. Maya: final asks for this pass: Ben to refine spacing and chips, Rach to add aria text proposals, Alex to confirm API mapping and countdown behavior, Simon to approve microcopy. I'll update figma and push a follow-up thread when ready. Alex: one more - for version history diff preview, can we show a 1-line diff summary (config keys changed) rather than full JSON? engineers love it, PMs love readability. Ben: yep — do a small expandable diff with monospace for keys and inline badges for changed/added/removed. deploy-bot: Deploy 5 -> production succeeded at 2024-11-02T15:07:12Z :rocket: (automated status) Simon: thanks everyone. will sync on the microcopy in tomorrow design review. :thumbsup:
